aspects.says: A subtype may accept more inputs and promise a narrower result; rejecting an input the supertype accepts or returning outside its promised range breaks callers written against the supertype.
basis: section:A Subtype May Accept More and Promise More, Never Less

aspects.says: A caller written against the supertype and run on every implementation is the only check of the contract; a test that uses one implementation checks only that one.
basis: section:javac Checks an Override's Signature; Only a Caller Run on Every Subtype Checks Its Contract
section:A Subtype May Accept More and Promise More, Never Less

aspects.says: javac rejects an override that declares a new checked exception or narrows access, but accepts one that throws a new unchecked exception or narrows what it accepts.
basis: section:javac Checks an Override's Signature; Only a Caller Run on Every Subtype Checks Its Contract
aspects.reason: a compile error is not something a practice's tests can grade; the page shows the javac run and the Reference table lists each case

aspects.says: List's mutators are optional operations, so an unmodifiable or fixed-size list keeps the contract by throwing, and a method that changes the list it was given is the code in breach; it builds a new list instead.
basis: section:List's Mutators Are Optional Operations, So the Caller That Changes Its Argument Is in Breach

aspects.says: Collection.contains may throw NullPointerException for a null query on a collection that holds no nulls, as List.of and Set.of do, while ArrayList answers false.
basis: section:List's Mutators Are Optional Operations, So the Caller That Changes Its Argument Is in Breach

aspects.says: Timestamp.equals refuses a Date while Date.equals accepts a Timestamp of the same millisecond, so a hash set or map of Dates keeps one or two entries depending on which arrived first; keying by Instant fixes it.
basis: section:Timestamp Breaks the Symmetry Object.equals Promises, So a Set of Dates Depends on Arrival Order
